title: PowerPoint on desktop: reference a Teams meeting or chat when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licence-assignment controls and documented data-protection limitations are supported. One minor correction is needed because the checklist asks readers to check deck protection without a corresponding control row.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Agent Mode in PowerPoint supports referencing a Teams meeting or chat when creating a presentation.
claims.quote: You can now reference a Teams meeting or chat when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot uses the referenced Teams meeting or chat as context to generate a presentation.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint can now use a referenced Teams meeting or chat as context when creating a presentation.

claims.claim: The release-notes entry is dated July 01, 2026.
claims.quote:
## July 01, 2026
Reference a Teams meeting or chat when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint

claims.claim: The documented procedure is to open PowerPoint, start Copilot, enter a prompt referencing the meeting or chat and press Enter.
claims.quote: Open PowerPoint and start Copilot. Enter a prompt that references the Teams meeting or chat you want to use in your presentation. Press Enter. Copilot will create a presentation using the referenced Teams content.

claims.claim: The release notes describe referencing meetings and chat messages securely.
claims.quote: This integration supports referencing meetings and chat messages securely within the presentation creation process.

claims.claim: The feature's release-notes entry does not explain how secure referencing is implemented.
claims.quote: This integration supports referencing meetings and chat messages securely within the presentation creation process.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The feature is user-opt-in: users choose to reference a Teams meeting or chat in their prompt.
claims.quote: Enter a prompt that references the Teams meeting or chat you want to use in your presentation. Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode reference Teams meeting chat admin disable setting policy Graph PowerShell 555884; no feature-specific enablement switch found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[0].governs; Cost and licensing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence gives access to the full Copilot experience in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft also documents an in-app PowerPoint Copilot experience for users without the add-on licence.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Some features in the experience without the add-on are subject to fair use limits.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps (for example, Word or Excel). It doesn't include full chat integration. Some features are subject to fair use limits.

claims.claim: Chat experiences in Word, Excel and PowerPoint vary with the user's licence and tenant configuration.
claims.quote: Chat experiences in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint vary depending on the user's license and tenant configuration.

claims.claim: The included licensing model represents a new option within licensed PowerPoint Copilot experiences, with feature-specific entitlement left qualified in the notes.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licence requirement specific to Teams meeting or chat references in PowerPoint Agent Mode is not published in the documentation found.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode Teams meetings chat references license billing meter prerequisites 555884; PowerPoint Teams meeting or chat license. Read feature release notes, Copilot overview and requirements; none names this feature's entitlement.

claims.claim: No meter specific to this feature is published in the documentation found.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode Teams meetings chat references license billing meter prerequisites 555884. Read release notes, Copilot overview including usage-based billing, and requirements; no meter for this feature was identified.

claims.claim: Licences can be assigned through Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign, then select Save changes.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the specified licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: Assign Microsoft 365 licenses to user accounts with the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK. To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Licence assignment requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: No documented tenant UI setting or automation call independently disables Teams meeting or chat references in PowerPoint Agent Mode.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode reference Teams meeting chat admin disable setting policy Graph PowerShell 555884; PowerPoint Agent Mode disable reference; PowerPoint Teams references Graph policy. Read release notes and privacy controls; results show only broader or unrelated controls.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot only summarises or references content the user is already authorised to access.
claims.quote: Permissions come first. Copilot only summarizes or references content that the user is already authorized to access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot and agents do not currently recognise sensitivity labels protecting Teams meetings and chats.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that protect Teams meetings and chat aren't currently recognized by Copilot and agents.

claims.claim: Those Teams meeting and chat sensitivity labels cannot be inherited by destination content.
claims.quote: data returned from a meeting chat or channel chat won't display an associated sensitivity label, copying chat data can't be prevented for a destination item, and the sensitivity label can't be inherited.

claims.claim: The label-recognition limitation does not apply to protected meeting invites, responses and calendar events.
claims.quote: This limitation doesn't apply to meeting invites, responses, and calendar events that are protected by sensitivity labels.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Connected-experience privacy controls can disable Copilot in desktop PowerPoint more broadly.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps: Excel OneNote Outlook PowerPoint Word

claims.claim: Assigning or removing the Copilot add-on affects the broader full PowerPoint Copilot experience rather than controlling only this feature.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote. You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: The release notes describe Copilot features generally as gradually rolling out within a tenant.
claims.quote: Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.

claims.claim: The feature's release-notes entry names no additional prerequisite beyond the described PowerPoint Copilot workflow.
claims.quote: Open PowerPoint and start Copilot. Enter a prompt that references the Teams meeting or chat you want to use in your presentation. Press Enter. Copilot will create a presentation using the referenced Teams content.

claims.claim: The feature's release-notes entry describes no action outside creating the presentation.
claims.quote: Press Enter. Copilot will create a presentation using the referenced Teams content.

claims.claim: Microsoft presents the feature as avoiding manual summarisation and transfer of Teams notes.
claims.quote: This makes it easier to turn Teams conversations, meeting outcomes, and chat discussions into presentation-ready content without manually summarizing or transferring notes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: PowerPoint content can carry sensitivity-label protection when the generated deck is shared.
claims.quote: Protect content in Office apps across different platforms and devices. Supported by Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook on the Office desktop apps and Office for the web.

claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote. Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode Teams meetings chat references license billing meter prerequisites 555884; no feature-specific charge found.

claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to check the generated deck's protection has no corresponding governance-control row.
